items.title: Chemistry Nobel recognizes work on how molecules acquire a single handedness
items.x_text:
Chemistry Nobel recognizes work on how molecules acquire a single handedness
Why does a molecule’s “handedness” matter to medicine?
#Cosmos #Chemistry #MolecularScience #NobelPrize
items.linkedin_text:
Chemistry Nobel recognizes work on how molecules acquire a single handedness

Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for discoveries involving autocatalysis and asymmetric synthesis. Their work helps explain how one molecular “hand” can become dominant—a property important in chemistry and drug development.

Molecular handedness can affect how substances behave in living systems, so methods for controlling it matter to pharmaceutical chemistry as well as fundamental questions about the chemistry of life.

What new medicines or insights into life’s origins could follow from better control of molecular handedness?

#Cosmos #ArtificialIntelligence #Investing #FinancialStability
items.linkedin_text:
AI boom brings financial and safety concerns into sharper focus

Investors and policymakers at Singapore forums on October 7 discussed risks from rapid AI investment, including high valuations, heavy borrowing and concerns about autonomous systems. The discussion reflects a widening debate about whether expected returns and safeguards will keep pace with investment.

If AI investment disappoints, losses could spread through markets and lenders; if deployment accelerates without adequate safeguards, the risks extend beyond finance. The overlap makes AI infrastructure both a technology and financial-stability issue.

What would happen if AI investment slowed before the infrastructure and safeguards were ready?

items.linkedin_text:
Italian firms plan €1 billion network of 13 data centers

Core Stack and Green Arrow Capital said they plan to invest more than €1 billion over four years to build 13 mid-sized data centers in Italy. The companies say the sites will use on-site renewable generation and an Italian supply chain; the first two are still awaiting permits.

A distributed, mid-sized approach could shape where digital infrastructure is built and how it connects to local power systems and suppliers. The projects also highlight the practical trade-offs between AI and cloud demand, permitting, and energy sourcing.

Could smaller, locally powered data centers ease—or intensify—pressure on regional infrastructure?

#Cosmos #Retail #Pharmacy #MergersAndAcquisitions
items.linkedin_text:
Weston family agrees to buy Boots in an $8.9 billion deal

Wittington Investments, the Weston family holding company, agreed to acquire Boots and related businesses from Sycamore Partners and the Pessina family. The deal covers Boots’ UK and Ireland retail operations, opticians and No7 beauty brand, and is expected to close in 2027 subject to regulatory approval.

The transaction returns a major pharmacy-and-retail chain to long-term family ownership and links Boots with a group that already operates Canadian grocery and pharmacy businesses. Its future investment choices could affect high-street retail and access to pharmacy services.

Could an owner with grocery and pharmacy experience change how Boots combines retail and healthcare?

items.linkedin_text:
Arctic sea ice ties for the satellite record’s tenth-lowest September minimum

NASA and the National Snow and Ice Data Center estimate Arctic sea ice covered 4.6 million square kilometers at its annual minimum on September 12, 2026, tying 2008, 2010 and 2025 for the tenth-lowest minimum in the satellite record. The area remains well below the long-term average despite a recent relative plateau.

The long-term decline and shift toward thinner, younger ice affect Arctic ecosystems and the region’s climate dynamics. The annual minimum is a useful measure of the broader trend, rather than a standalone indicator of any single year’s conditions.

How might a thinner, younger Arctic ice cover change the region’s ecosystems and climate feedbacks?
